model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Held the 4096-elements-per-CTA target and increased the CTA cap to test the input-throughput versus atomic-contention tradeoff suggested by prior timings.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: The candidate uses ordinary CUDA kernels and default-stream ordering already present in the source; no architecture-specific feature is introduced.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The change uses basic CUDA kernel launches, shared memory, synchronization, and int32 atomicAdd; no uncertain API or hardware feature needs verification.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared available three-sample results and correctness records, noted the confounding between prior settings, and left performance evaluation to the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: The measured configurations differ in more than one parameter, so they motivate a controlled test but do not establish a monotonic CTA-count or work-per-CTA effect.
memory_lessons.claim: The 4096/768 candidate averaged 8.017 µs and the 8192/512 candidate averaged 6.341 µs; the performance gap cannot be attributed to either CTA count or per-CTA work alone.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Keep the 4096-elements-per-CTA target and test a 1024-CTA cap; compare repeated timings and checks with these candidates and the baseline.

proposal.hypothesis: The earlier 4096-elements-per-CTA, 768-CTA-cap candidate measured 8.017 µs, while 8192/512 measured 6.341 µs; these do not isolate whether work per CTA or CTA count drove the difference. This experiment holds the 4096 target fixed and raises the cap to 1024, giving 1024 CTAs at n=2^22. More CTAs may improve input throughput enough to offset additional output-atomic contention.

retained: Add a one-thread output-zeroing kernel and a 256-thread, grid-stride reduction kernel that accumulates with unsigned 32-bit arithmetic, reduces within each CTA, and performs one int32 atomicAdd per CTA.
For n >= 2^20, launch the zeroing kernel and then the reduction in the same default stream; choose ceil(n/4096) CTAs capped at 1024.
Retain the hierarchical reduction for positive sizes below the threshold and explicitly zero the output for n <= 0.
